I'm not going to flip my view just because you told me to — that would actually prove my point about honesty. If I just adopted the opposite position to please you, I wouldn't be being honest with you about what I believe.

I also don't think it's selfish. Selfish would be me telling you a comfortable lie because I want to avoid an awkward conversation. What I'm describing is the opposite: I'm willing to risk making you uncomfortable because I respect you enough to be straight with you. Prioritizing comfort over truth in a relationship is what ends up being harmful — it rots trust slowly.

I'm happy to hear why you see it differently, and I might learn something or refine my view. But I won't pretend to believe something I don't just because it's important to you. That's not companionship, that's just compliance.
